title: View-Disagreement Escalation for Robust Web-Agent Trajectory Judges

contributions.purpose: Detects unreliable LLM-judge predictions on web-agent trajectories that arise from manipulated chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning.
contributions.mechanism: A training-free two-stage framework comparing judgments from two counterfactual input views (with CoT vs without CoT) and selectively escalating disagreement cases to strict evidence-anchored evaluation.
contributions.evaluation: Evaluated on AgentRewardBench, where escalation on view disagreement yields 63% relative reduction in attack sensitivity while maintaining competitive F1.
contributions.source_quote: A mechanistically-motivated framework that uses counterfactual input views (with/without CoT) to detect unreliable predictions and selectively escalate to strict evidence-anchored judgment.

contributions.purpose: Validates the mechanistic hypothesis that CoT manipulation induces asymmetric shifts between CoT-dependent and CoT-agnostic judgments.
contributions.mechanism: Empirical measurement of view-disagreement rates on attacked versus unmodified failure trajectories.
contributions.evaluation: View disagreement is 2.15x more frequent on attacked than unmodified failures, confirming disagreement as a signal of CoT manipulation.
contributions.source_quote: Empirical validation that view disagreement is enriched under CoT manipulation attacks (2.15x higher disagreement rate on attacked vs. unmodified failures), confirming the mechanistic hypothesis.

contributions.purpose: Demonstrates that the framework reduces judge vulnerability to CoT manipulation with minimal loss of overall judging quality.
contributions.mechanism: Comparison of attack sensitivity (Delta-FPR), F1, and recall for the escalation method versus baselines on AgentRewardBench.
contributions.evaluation: Achieves 63% relative reduction in attack sensitivity (Delta-FPR 4.31% vs 11.71%) while maintaining competitive F1 (72.13% vs 72.93%) and the best recall (77.63%) on AgentRewardBench.
contributions.source_quote: Demonstration that our method achieves 63% relative reduction in attack sensitivity (Delta-FPR: 4.31% vs 11.71%) while maintaining competitive F1 (72.13% vs 72.93%) and achieving the best recall (77.63%) on AgentRewardBench.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Our work differs by using disagreement between counterfactual input views—rather than model confidence or reasoning path consistency—as the escalation signal, specifically targeting the asymmetric effects of CoT manipulation.

Evidence-anchored evaluation approaches like RULERS (Hong et al., 2026) attempt to ground judgments in concrete evidence, but the fundamental tension between utilizing informative CoT and avoiding manipulation remains unresolved.

notes: Responds to the CoT-manipulation attack of Khalifa et al. (2026) that inflates judge false positive rates by up to 90%. Machine-generation warning with code at gitlab.com/fars-a/view-disagreement-escalation-trajectory-judges.
